launch_timeline_rationale: SKG0106 is clinically active but still early. Without a pivotal Phase 3 or filing signal, a U.S. launch before 2030 is unlikely; long-term follow-up reinforces unresolved safety and durability questions.
annual_cost_rationale: SKG0106 is a one-time ocular AAV therapy, so a one-time per-eye gene therapy analog is more relevant than annualizing chronic anti-VEGF injections. phase: Phase 2 long-term extension; completed Phase 2b parent study; J&J's April 2026 development pipeline lists JNJ-1887 sCD59 for geographic atrophy in Phase 2.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT06635148 as a recruiting Phase 2 long-term extension of JNJ-81201887 parent studies in participants with geographic atrophy secondary to AMD. The extension started on 2024-09-19, estimates enrollment of 274, has estimated primary completion on 2029-08-24 and estimated study completion on 2030-07-16, and gives no study intervention in the LTE. The randomized Phase 2b parent study NCT05811351 completed on 2026-02-23 with actual enrollment of 305, but no ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted. J&J's current pipeline still places JNJ-1887 sCD59 in Phase 2, with no disclosed filing or launch timing.
expected_launch_window: 2031 or later unless Janssen advances using the completed Phase 2b dataset on an accelerated or otherwise shortened regulatory path
launch_timeline_display: 2031 or later unless Janssen advances using the completed Phase 2b dataset on an accelerated or otherwise shortened regulatory path
expected_launch_rationale: A near-term launch is not source-supported. The program could move faster if the completed Phase 2b study is treated as registrational or triggers an expedited path, but public sources currently support monitoring as a Phase 2 asset with long-term safety follow-up extending to 2030.
launch_timeline_rationale: A near-term launch is not source-supported. The program could move faster if the completed Phase 2b study is treated as registrational or triggers an expedited path, but public sources currently support monitoring as a Phase 2 asset with long-term safety follow-up extending to 2030.
annual_cost_rationale: No JNJ-81201887 price exists. The low end reflects the annual one-eye cost of an approved intravitreal GA complement inhibitor; the high end reflects a one-time ocular gene therapy WAC per eye. The range excludes rebates, medical administration, imaging, corticosteroid prophylaxis, anti-VEGF rescue, bilateral treatment, facility fees, and outcomes-based contracting.
risk_rationale: Operational disruption is not imminent, but the asset could alter current repeated-injection GA pathways and medical-benefit contracting if controlled data support durable benefit.
action_rationale: Monitor for Phase 2b readout and regulatory-path clarity before drafting final coverage policy; maintain early scenario notes for one-time ophthalmic gene therapy pricing and outcomes-based contracting.

development_status: NCT06223958/SOL-1 is an active-not-recruiting Phase 3 superiority trial in treatment-naive wet AMD with 344 actual randomized subjects. Ocular reported positive Week 36 and Week 52 SOL-1 data in February 2026 and states that an NDA based on SOL-1 Week 52 data remains on track, subject to ongoing or planned formal FDA discussions. A second Phase 3 wet AMD trial, NCT06495918/SOL-R, is active not recruiting and is expected by the company to read out in 1Q 2027.
expected_launch_window: Potential U.S. 2027 launch if NDA submission, FDA acceptance, review, and approval proceed on the company's planned SOL-1-based path; timing remains contingent on FDA discussions and review.
launch_timeline_display: Potential U.S. 2027 launch if NDA submission, FDA acceptance, review, and approval proceed on the company's planned SOL-1-based path; timing remains contingent on FDA discussions and review.
expected_launch_rationale: A 2027 window is plausible because SOL-1 is positive and Ocular is preparing an NDA, but the packet should not assume approval before FDA accepts the filing path, reviews the single-trial package, and resolves CMC/label questions.
launch_timeline_rationale: A 2027 window is plausible because SOL-1 is positive and Ocular is preparing an NDA, but the packet should not assume approval before FDA accepts the filing path, reviews the single-trial package, and resolves CMC/label questions.
annual_cost_rationale: This is a gross drug-acquisition planning proxy, not a forecast of AXPAXLI list price or net payer cost. Final cost may differ materially if Ocular prices the durable implant at a premium to annual anti-VEGF drug spend, if bilateral use is common, or if rescue aflibercept and administration costs are included.
risk_rationale: AXPAXLI could materially change wet AMD treatment cadence and payer controls if approved. Disruption is high despite remaining regulatory uncertainty because commercial preparedness and pivotal data are already in place.
action_rationale: Begin draft coverage and operations planning now, while keeping assumptions provisional until FDA filing status, label, pricing, HCPCS/J-code strategy, SOL-R data, and launch timing are clarified.

phase: Phase 2 program; assigned NCT06707753 is Phase 1/2a and related NCT06839339 is Phase 2
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT06707753 as an active, not recruiting, open-label, nonrandomized, single-dose, dose-escalation Phase 1/2a study of AL-001 suprachoroidal injection in 21 patients with wet AMD; estimated primary and final completion were 2025-08-31 and no results are posted. The related randomized, positive-controlled Phase 2 study NCT06839339 plans 40 patients randomized to two AL-001 dose cohorts or aflibercept, with estimated primary completion 2026-09-30 and estimated final completion 2027-01-30. A linked long-term follow-up study, NCT06718816, follows AL-001-treated patients through an estimated 2029-06-30 completion.
expected_launch_window: China 2030+ if Phase 2 and later registrational data support approval; U.S. launch not forecast without FDA/US trial signal
launch_timeline_display: China 2030+ if Phase 2 and later registrational data support approval; U.S. launch not forecast without FDA/US trial signal
expected_launch_rationale: AL-001 has advanced into a Phase 2 aflibercept-controlled China study, but pivotal evidence, filing guidance, and U.S. regulatory signals are not yet public. A China-first 2030+ watch window is more defensible than near-term launch planning.
launch_timeline_rationale: AL-001 has advanced into a Phase 2 aflibercept-controlled China study, but pivotal evidence, filing guidance, and U.S. regulatory signals are not yet public. A China-first 2030+ watch window is more defensible than near-term launch planning.
annual_cost_rationale: AL-001 is described publicly as an ocular AAV anti-VEGF gene therapy, so a one-time per-eye ocular gene therapy analog is more relevant than annualizing chronic anti-VEGF injections. Final AL-001 price could differ materially based on China pricing, U.S. launch status, durability, bilateral use, rebates, payment model, and administration costs.
risk_rationale: The mechanism could be disruptive if durable and safe, but near-term operational disruption is low because AL-001 remains pre-pivotal publicly and has no identified U.S. launch pathway.
action_rationale: Monitor Phase 2 activation/completion, BCVA and CRT results, rescue anti-VEGF frequency, ocular inflammation/immunogenicity signals, long-term follow-up, and any U.S. IND or partner activity before preparing policy build.

development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NOVA-1 (NCT05769153) as an active, not recruiting Phase 1/2 two-stage study in neovascular age-related macular degeneration. Stage 1 included an open-label lower-dose cohort receiving one aflibercept 2 mg injection at Week -1 and one AR-14034 SR lower-dose intravitreal insertion at baseline, with up to one AR-14034 SR retreatment between Weeks 4 and 36 based on disease activity. Stage 2 randomizes participants to one or two AR-14034 SR insertions versus labeled aflibercept. Actual enrollment is 139, estimated primary completion is May 2027, estimated study completion is October 2027, and no ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.
expected_launch_rationale: A launch before 2031 is unlikely unless the Phase 1/2 study produces unusually registrational evidence or Alcon accelerates directly into a rapid pivotal program after 2027.
launch_timeline_rationale: A launch before 2031 is unlikely unless the Phase 1/2 study produces unusually registrational evidence or Alcon accelerates directly into a rapid pivotal program after 2027.
annual_cost_rationale: AR-14034 SR has no disclosed price. The range anchors to current nAMD durable anti-VEGF drug acquisition and sustained-delivery implant analogs, excluding administration, surgery/procedure fees, imaging, office visits, adverse-event management, rebates, discounts, and supplemental rescue injections.
risk_rationale: AR-14034 SR could alter visit and injection burden if durable, but the near-term risk is limited by lack of results and likely need for pivotal development.
action_rationale: Monitor NOVA-1 results, dose selection, and pivotal-trial plans before drafting product-specific policy; retain general anti-VEGF/implant management concepts for launch readiness.

phase: Early Phase 1 for assigned IIT record NCT06888492; separate EXG202-111 record NCT07178249 is Phase 1/2.
development_status: NCT06888492 is a not-yet-recruiting, open-label, non-randomized, sequential dose-escalation Early Phase 1 study in China evaluating two intravitreal EXG202 dose cohorts in 8 participants with wet/neovascular AMD; estimated start is 2025-03-28, estimated primary completion is 2026-04-25, estimated study completion is 2026-04-30, and no results are posted. A separate EXG202 Phase 1/2 study, NCT07178249, is also not yet recruiting, plans 60 participants, has estimated start 2025-10-16, estimated primary completion 2028-02-28, and estimated study completion 2032-12-30. Exegenesis/Jiayin's HKEX application proof states EXG202 received FDA IND clearance in July 2025 and NMPA IND approval in August 2025, and that an IIT was being conducted for early safety, tolerability, and biological-activity insights.

launch_timeline_display: 2033 or later unless Phase 1/2 data support an accelerated or otherwise shortened regulatory path
expected_launch_rationale: A near-term launch is not source-supported. EXG202 has IND clearance and early clinical activity, but current public records support a long development path with Phase 1/2 follow-up extending to 2032 before any standard late-stage filing pathway.
launch_timeline_rationale: A near-term launch is not source-supported. EXG202 has IND clearance and early clinical activity, but current public records support a long development path with Phase 1/2 follow-up extending to 2032 before any standard late-stage filing pathway.

development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT07607561 as a not-yet-recruiting Phase 2a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel, multicenter study in neovascular wet AMD. The trial will randomize 50 subjects 2:2:1 to SCAI-005 0.04%, SCAI-005 0.08%, or placebo, with estimated start on 2026-11-01 and estimated primary/study completion on 2027-08-31. SCAI and Korean industry coverage report Phase 1 completion and Korean MFDS Phase 2 IND approval in May 2026.
expected_launch_window: 2031-2033+ if Phase 2a is positive and a partner-backed pivotal program succeeds; no defined U.S. launch path.
launch_timeline_display: 2031-2033+ if Phase 2a is positive and a partner-backed pivotal program succeeds; no defined U.S. launch path.
expected_launch_rationale: The asset is early Phase 2a, not yet recruiting, and SCAI has publicly discussed Phase 2 evaluation and external collaboration rather than a direct launch timeline.
launch_timeline_rationale: The asset is early Phase 2a, not yet recruiting, and SCAI has publicly discussed Phase 2 evaluation and external collaboration rather than a direct launch timeline.
annual_cost_rationale: No SCAI-005 price, bottle size, days supply, or net cost exists. Because SCAI-005 is intended to affect wet AMD injection burden, branded anti-VEGF WAC provides a conservative wet AMD analog, not a forecast of final topical axitinib pricing.
risk_rationale: Operational disruption would be meaningful if topical SCAI-005 reduces injection frequency, but Phase 2a has not started and no patient efficacy data are available.
action_rationale: No active formulary build is warranted yet; reassess when Phase 2a recruitment, CST/BCVA results, safety, dosing, partnering, and regulatory plans become public.

development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT06832657 as a not-yet-recruiting, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 study of single and multiple ascending doses of JMKX003948 Ophthalmic Suspension in 40 healthy adults. The trial lists AMD and DME as conditions, uses 1%, 2%, 3%, and 5% suspension strengths, and measures AEs, ophthalmic examination changes, and plasma PK through Day 14. The record was last updated February 18, 2025, with estimated start February 2025 and estimated primary/study completion December 2025, but no posted results were available and the status remained not yet recruiting in the reviewed CT.gov API snapshot. A separate JMKX003948 tablet Phase 1 RCC study, NCT06321250, is recruiting in China and supports broader clinical activity for the molecule but not ophthalmic efficacy.
expected_launch_window: 2031+ / uncertain
launch_timeline_display: 2031+ / uncertain
expected_launch_rationale: A near-term launch is not supportable. Even if development resumes, JMKX003948 would need patient dose-ranging, comparative efficacy, longer safety, and registrational evidence before an AMD/DME approval.
launch_timeline_rationale: A near-term launch is not supportable. Even if development resumes, JMKX003948 would need patient dose-ranging, comparative efficacy, longer safety, and registrational evidence before an AMD/DME approval.
annual_cost_rationale: This is a gross drug-acquisition analog before rebates, discounts, administration fees, bilateral treatment, adherence, or topical-pricing differences. A topical small molecule could price below, near, or above injectable analogs depending on final efficacy and positioning.
risk_rationale: Operational disruption is low now. The risk should be revisited if Jemincare posts patient efficacy data, starts a Phase 2 AMD/DME trial, or demonstrates injection-sparing outcomes.
action_rationale: Monitor CT.gov status changes, Phase 1 completion/results, patient AMD/DME study starts, mechanism confirmation from Jemincare or regulators, and any U.S. development signal before preparing policy criteria.
